method.value: Inspect images with CASA Viewer; imstat peak within 1'' aperture and rms in 1.0-1.2'' annulus

evidence.loc: 3.1 Continuum images, disc photometry, and sizes
evidence.quote: We first used the *imstat* task to search for the peak flux value within an aperture of 1$''$ in radius and calculated an rms from an annulus with an inner and outer radius of 1.0$''$ and 1.2$''$.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit fluxes and sizes of single sources in the uv plane

method.value: uvmodelfit point source and Gaussian fits for single objects with peak S/N>5; resolved only if S/N>30 and Gaussian flux > point flux + 3 rms; elliptical disc model for substructured sources

evidence.loc: 3.1 Continuum images, disc photometry, and sizes
evidence.quote: we provide size information only if the source has a peak S/N $>$ 30 and the Gaussian flux is greater than the point source flux plus 3 times the rms of the sky between 1 and 1.2$''$ of the target.

findings_qualitative.value: Dust mass distribution in Ophiuchus is similar to other young (1-2 Myr) regions such as Taurus and Lupus

evidence.quote: We find that the dust mass distribution in our Ophiuchus sample (which is not yet complete) is very similar to those of other young regions (1-2 Myr) as Taurus and Lupus.

findings_qualitative.value: Brighter discs tend to be larger but with ~factor 10 dispersion; discs with close companions tend to be small

evidence.quote: There is a tendency for brighter discs to be larger, but the flux vs size relation show a significant dispersion (a factor of $\sim$10).

claims.hypothesis: Do Ophiuchus discs have enough dust mass to form planets?
claims.experiment: Convert 1.3 mm fluxes to dust masses with standard assumptions
claims.result: All detected discs have M_dust >~0.5 Earth masses; only ~50 have ~10 Earth masses
claims.finding: All detected discs can form rocky planets; only ~1/3 can form gas-giant cores

evidence.quote: all discs detected at 1.3 mm are massive enough to form one or more rocky planets.

claims.hypothesis: Are substructures common among bright discs?
claims.experiment: Self-calibrated uniform-weight images and deprojected radial profiles
claims.result: 8 clear and 4 possible substructures, all among the brightest sources
claims.finding: ~28% (7/25) of the brightest, and up to ~50% of >50 mJy sources may show substructure

evidence.quote: This implies that $\sim$28$\%$ (7/25) of the brightest objects show some type of substructures when observed at $\sim$0.2$''$ ($\sim$28 au) resolution.

claims.hypothesis: What is the typical disc size and brightness distribution?
claims.experiment: Fit sizes of resolved sources, set unresolved at FWHM 0.2''
claims.result: Most discs radii <15 au; ~15% have >30 au
claims.finding: Disc population is dominated by compact, faint discs

evidence.quote: most detected discs have radii $<$ 15 au, while only 23 discs ($\sim$15$\%$ of the targets) have radii $>$ 30 au.
